Global Times: Xi stresses sustained efforts to expand, strengthen advanced manufacturing
articles.desc: BEIJING , Sept. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged sustained efforts to expand and strengthen advanced manufacturing to provide strong support for advancing Chinese modernization. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chai
articles.content: BEIJING , Sept. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged sustained efforts to expand and strengthen advanced manufacturing to provide strong support for advancing Chinese modernization. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a recent instruction, which was conveyed at a national conference on advanced manufacturing held in Beijing on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the Xinhua News Agency. Efforts should be made to ensure both high-quality development and greater security, pursue smart, green and integrated development, and make the country's industrial chains more self-supporting and risk-resilient, Xi stressed, Xinhua reported. The remarks come as advanced manufacturing is taking on a larger role in underpinning China's industrial growth and driving structural upgrading. In the first eight months of the year, value-added industrial output of major enterprises increased 5.3 percent year-on-year, while that of high-tech manufacturing rose 14.2 percent. Experts said that smart, green and integrated developments together chart the key direction for China's manufacturing upgrade, with intelligent technologies providing the foundation, green development shaping long-term competitiveness, and deeper integration helping traditional industries accelerate transformation. They added that the push will also help strengthen China's indigenous capabilities in key technologies and make industrial and supply chains more independent and resilient, while maintaining openness to global industrial cooperation. Key directions for upgrading Xi emphasized the need to accelerate the development of a modernized industrial system with advanced manufacturing as the backbone, and reinforce the foundations of the real economy. Premier Li Qiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, delivered a speech at the conference, Xinhua reported. Xi's important instructions provide essential guidance for developing advanced manufacturing, Li said, noting that China must treat developing advanced manufacturing as a major strategic task, and press steadily to boost its strength in manufacturing. Bian Yongzu, executive deputy editor-in-chief of Modernization of Management magazine, told the Global Times that smart development provides the technological foundation, with AI, big data, intelligent equipment and robotics increasingly embedded in production to improve efficiency, precision and automation. Green development points to the long-term direction, as lower-carbon and more resource-efficient production becomes an increasingly important part of industrial competitiveness, he explained. Integrated development, Bian said, is especially relevant to China's vast manufacturing base. China has both advanced factories and a large number of traditional industries that remain essential to the economy. The key is not simply to replace traditional manufacturing, but to upgrade it by bringing intelligent and green technologies into existing production systems. Chen Jing, vice president of the Technology and Strategy Research Institute, told the Global Times that the different dimensions of manufacturing upgrading reinforce each other. Intelligent technologies can serve as a common lever, supporting both technological upgrading and emissions reduction, while green development creates new demand for higher-end technologies. Stronger technological capabilities and higher value-added production can in turn support further investment in intelligent and green transformation. Chen also said competition in advanced manufacturing will go beyond production capacity and prices. Innovation capability, industrial security, product quality and branding, as well as low-carbon capabilities, will become crucial measures of competitiveness. The broader shift, he said, is from factor-driven growth toward innovation-driven development, and from advantages in individual products toward stronger industrial ecosystems and a higher position in global value chains. He added that moving in these directions will also help strengthen China's technological self-reliance, reduce excessive reliance on external sources in key areas, and improve its ability to make breakthroughs in critical technologies. China's advantages include its vast domestic market, complete industrial system, strong engineering workforce and rich application scenarios, Chen said. The large market gives companies room to test and improve new products quickly, while dense supply chains and a broad manufacturing base help shorten the path from R&D to mass production. Self-reliance, however, does not mean cutting China off from global industrial cooperation, Chen said. A more realistic path is to strengthen the substitutability of key technologies and improve supply-chain resilience, while continuing to participate in international cooperation and global markets. Breakthroughs across advanced manufacturing Smart, green and integrated upgrading is already taking shape across China's manufacturing sector, as emerging technologies move faster into industrial application. The Global Times learned from AGIBOT that its Genie G2 humanoid robot has been deployed on a tablet production line in Nanchang, East China's Jiangxi Province, where it performs precision loading and unloading tasks with a reported success rate of 99 percent. Yao Maoqing, co-founder of AGIBOT and chairman and CEO of Maniformer Technology, told the Global Times that embodied intelligence is a typical example of the deep integration of AI and advanced manufacturing. China's rich manufacturing scenarios, complete industrial system and growing innovation capacity could accelerate the transition of embodied intelligence from technological breakthroughs to large-scale applications, he said. The expansion of robotics into real production is not confined to factory assembly lines. DEEP Robotics told the Global Times that it is integrating AI with motion control, environmental perception and autonomous navigation, while deploying robots in energy, power inspection, emergency response and other complex environments. As Chinese robotic technologies enter a wider range of industrial scenarios, the company said it is also adapting its products and services to overseas markets and building local partnerships. Behind the expanding applications is an increasingly complete industrial ecosystem. Shenzhen's "Robot Valley," covering about 28 square kilometers, has gathered more than 200 robotics-related companies, including more than 25 humanoid robot manufacturers. Its industrial chain stretches from AI models, tactile sensors and lidar to servo motors, joint modules, robotic arms and dexterous hands, with the localization rate of key components exceeding 90 percent. The momentum seen in robotics is part of a broader acceleration across China's advanced manufacturing sector. In August, value-added output of equipment manufacturing rose 12.1 percent year-on-year, while high-tech manufacturing expanded 16.7 percent. New growth drivers, led by high-tech manufacturing and digital product manufacturing, contributed more than 60 percent of the growth in industrial output that month. Industrial robot output jumped 34.6 percent year-on-year. Besides robotics, recent advances have also extended in other fields. The CR450 high-speed train has completed whole-vehicle testing; the Zhuque-3 Y2 reusable carrier rocket achieved a land recovery of its first stage; and China's second domestically built large cruise ship, Adora Flora City, is scheduled for delivery in November. The transformation is also becoming greener. During the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-30), China plans to cultivate 500 zero-carbon factories and develop replicable models, while pushing traditional industries including steel, nonferrous metals and petrochemicals to adopt cleaner raw materials and fuels, optimize product structures and integrate low-carbon technologies. China will also improve standards for green factories, green supply chains and green industrial parks. By 2030, output from green factories at all levels is targeted to account for 45 percent of the total output of major manufacturing enterprises. Bian Yongzu told the Global Times that China's expanding advanced manufacturing capacity is increasingly translating into stronger global competitiveness. As Chinese manufacturers improve technological capabilities, efficiency and product quality, they are not only meeting increasingly diversified domestic demand, but also supplying more high-tech and cost-effective products to overseas markets, he said. He said this reflects a broader shift in Chinese manufacturing from scale expansion toward higher technological content and stronger competitiveness, while creating more opportunities for industrial cooperation with other countries.

articles.title: Bruce Spangenberg column: Plan for spring flowers now
articles.desc: Choose the proper location and spring-flowering bulbs are dependable to be productive year after year.
articles.content: Bruce Spangenberg column: Plan for spring flowers now - Superior Telegram | News, weather, sports from Superior Wisconsin Bruce Spangenberg column: Plan for spring flowers now Choose the proper location and spring-flowering bulbs are dependable to be productive year after year. Unpaid content from readers. Lightly edited. Spring-flowering bulbs providing dependable splashes of color are a welcome sight as winter fades, and now is the time to plan for a dazzling landscape display next spring. Following just a few simple guidelines for planting this fall provides great color every spring. Bulbs purchased to plant this fall, or already in place in the landscape, have everything packed away for growing next spring. Energy to break dormancy, grow shoots and develop flowers is produced and stored the prior growing season. This is why one important rule of spring flowering bulb care is to allow leaves to remain after bloom each year. These green leaves take in sunlight and convert to storable energy. Bulbs grown in production nurseries for sale this fall have gone through this same process. Spring-flowering bulb structures are remarkably similar to seeds. Like seeds, there is a dormant living portion that becomes the growing plant, stored energy, and some sort of protective cover. Examples include true bulbs such as tulips, narcissus (daffodils), snowdrops and hyacinth, along with corms such as crocus. When choosing at garden center outlets, look for healthy, unblemished structures and avoid those that are off-color, soft and diseased. Smaller yet healthy looking bulbs mixed in with larger ones of the same kind may not flower the first spring after planting. Choose the proper location and spring-flowering bulbs are dependable to be productive year after year. Good soil drainage is the first critical criteria for planting sites; sitting in wet soils is the one big reason plantings may fail. Heavier clay soils can be amended with organic matter, such as compost, peat or rotted manure, to depth of about 8 inches. Likewise, adding these materials to excessively dry sandy soils can help hold more moisture. Ensuring there will be adequate sunlight during the period after bloom is a second key criteria for planting sites. It allows green leaves to produce the energy needed for ongoing success. Oftentimes those that bloom early planted under shade trees have enough time before the tree foliage develops and casts significant shade. Bulbs planted in excessively shaded sites, however, may decline each successive year because of insufficient sunlight available. Bruce Spangenberg column: Bluestems enhance fall landscape Bruce Spangenberg column: Aerating and overseeding lawns Squirrels digging up recently fall planted bulbs is often an issue. One remedy is spreading poultry wire just under the soil surface after planting. This prevents squirrels from digging them up. Next spring shoots will easily emerge through the holes in the buried wire. Do some research on all spring-flowering bulb choices and their bloom time. With some planning, landscapes may have continuous color displays from early to late spring. Bruce Spangenberg is a horticulture outreach specialist with UW-Madison Division of Extension. articles.title: North Monroe Street Grocery Ditches Fresh 4 Less Name for Piggly Wiggly Food for Less
articles.desc: Tallahassee's North Monroe Street Fresh 4 Less has rebranded as Piggly Wiggly Food for Less, keeping its cost-plus pricing model intact.
articles.content: Fresh 4 Less Becomes Piggly Wiggly in Tallahassee North Monroe Street Grocery Ditches Fresh 4 Less Name for Piggly Wiggly Food for Less 2526 S Monroe St. — Other Piggly Wiggly Location The grocery store at 3813 North Monroe St. in Tallahassee has a new name on the marquee. Fresh 4 Less, the budget grocer that has served the Lake Jackson area since 2018, is now operating as Piggly Wiggly Food for Less, according to the local grocery store's Facebook post announcing the conversion earlier this month. The rebrand folds the North Monroe location into a fast-growing regional chain owned by Sneads-based McDaniel Family Investments, Inc., as reported by the . The store had operated as an affiliate of Piggly Wiggly under the Fresh 4 Less banner, but it now carries the Piggly Wiggly name outright, joining a network that spans 14 supermarket locations across North Florida, central and south Georgia, and the Montgomery, Alabama market as of August 2026, according to . The company traces its roots back to 1989, when William Ralph McDaniel bought a local IGA grocery store before shifting to the Piggly Wiggly brand in the early 1990s; it's now run by brothers Kevin and Cody McDaniel. Despite the new sign, the store's pricing structure isn't changing. Store management said the cost-plus model has created significant savings for customers without compromising quality, per the Tallahassee Democrat's reporting. Under that setup, goods are sold at cost plus 10 percent to cover operational expenses and overhead — a pricing quirk that can catch shoppers used to conventional retail tags off guard, though it's designed to pass savings straight through to buyers. The North Monroe store occupies 50,000 square feet and sells produce, meats, seafood and shelf items, preparing fruits and vegetables fresh daily and offering a wash-and-cut service on produce. It's now the second Piggly Wiggly Food for Less location in Tallahassee, joining a store at 2526 S. Monroe St. on the city's southside. The North Monroe location is open 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Sunday through Friday and 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. on Saturdays. A Truckload Meat Blowout and a Broader Push on Protein Prices The rebrand landed just days after the store hosted a truckload meat blowout on September 17, featuring ground beef, Certified Angus prime top sirloin and pork, according to the Tallahassee Democrat. That sale fits into a larger regional push: in August 2026, Piggly Wiggly Food for Less rolled out an Affordable Protein Initiative across all 14 of its locations, offering discounted pricing on fresh beef, pork and poultry that was developed through direct negotiations with meat manufacturers, according to The company isn't slowing its expansion, either. Piggly Wiggly Food for Less has plans for six locations across Alabama, Georgia and Florida, including sites in Havana, Wetumpka, Montgomery, Sandersville and Eastman, per the Tallahassee Democrat. The chain already operates a Piggly Wiggly Food for Less store in Sneads, while Havana is among its planned locations across the surrounding Big Bend and Panhandle region, and it opened a location in Gadsden County in December. The North Monroe site has carried outsized importance for the Lake Jackson neighborhood since it first opened as Fresh 4 Less on September 8, 2018. At the time, the store employed more than 100 people and featured amenities like an on-site produce butcher and a hot food bar, according to the . Its opening restored grocery access for residents who had faced a retail void after Winn-Dixie reduced its brick-and-mortar presence across Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina and South Carolina that same year, closing 94 stores in the process. The Piggly Wiggly name itself carries more than a century of grocery history. articles.title: ONEflight Suspends Flights, Leaving Jet-Card Customers Awaiting Answers
articles.desc: ONEflight International, based near Centennial Airport, paused flights and deleted social media as customers say $150 million in prepaid deposits is at risk.
articles.content: ONEflight Pauses Flights, Deletes Accounts in Colorado ONEflight Suspends Flights, Leaving Jet-Card Customers Awaiting Answers ONEflight International has paused its flight arrangements for at least 30 days, or until it provides further notice, while the Colorado-based charter broker reviews its operations. The company, which works near Centennial Airport, has also removed its Facebook and Instagram accounts. Customer calls went unanswered Friday, and chief operating executive Ferren Rajput was unavailable for comment, according to The size of the customer exposure is still an estimate Doug Gollan, editor of Private Jet Card Comparisons, told The Denver Post that customers had paid ONEflight more than $150 million for future travel through its jet-card program. That figure represents reported prepaid exposure, not a confirmed loss, and the article's available reporting does not establish that customers will forfeit those balances. ONEflight sells jet cards and arranges trips with outside pilots and charter operators rather than operating the aircraft itself. Customers may pay $100,000 or more in advance, while the broker later uses those funds to obtain individual flights. Forbes reported that customer money was not placed in escrow, and Live and Let's Fly described how prepaid funds could therefore be available for broader business needs rather than being reserved exclusively for each customer's future trip: Earlier transactions add financial context Reports published before and around the suspension describe several developments at the company, although none of them alone establishes why flights were halted. Live and Let's Fly reported that ONEflight sold $2.29 million in future credit-card receivables for $1.65 million in July. Private Jet Card Comparisons reported that the company announced a 35 percent economic surcharge for jet-card members on Aug. 25 and withdrew it hours later after customers objected: Live and Let's Fly also reported that multiple outside charter operators faced six-figure unpaid balances for completed flights. Forbes reported that ONEflight had recorded $232 million in revenue in 2025, a 90 percent year-over-year increase. That revenue figure does not show the company's profit, cash position or ability to meet future customer obligations. The cause of the interruption has not been established Johannes Uys, identified as ONEflight's chief financial officer as recently as May 2026, was arrested in July on domestic-violence-related charges and is now in immigration detention in Aurora, according to court records cited by The Denver Post. An internal September email from Human Resources Vice President Ruby Dalton, reported by Aviation International News, said Rajput was addressing financial and operational problems that developed under the previous CFO. The email did not explain specifically what led to the flight pause. If ONEflight enters bankruptcy, jet-card customers would generally be treated as unsecured creditors, according to Private Jet Card Comparisons. They could then compete with other claimants for whatever assets remained. Whether the company will reorganize, file for bankruptcy or resume arranging flights is still unknown. For now, the suspension remains in effect for at least 30 days or until further notice. articles.title: Provo Nursing Student, 22, Runs Marathons Through Rare Terminal Brain Cancer Fight
articles.desc: Alex Perry, 22, of Provo has terminal brain cancer far younger than typical. She's running marathons and finishing nursing school anyway.
articles.content: Provo Woman, 22, Fights Rare Brain Cancer, Runs Marathons Provo Nursing Student, 22, Runs Marathons Through Rare Terminal Brain Cancer Fight Alex Rowan is 22, completing nursing school and training for a second marathon while being treated for high-grade astrocytoma with piloid features, a rare and aggressive brain tumor. She has continued running during radiation and chemotherapy, wearing the words “Lift the Odds” on her forearm and on each race bib. Rowan's diagnosis came in 2025, after months of migraines that affected her vision and headaches that started in the winter of 2024, according to . A CT scan revealed a mass, and doctors told her it was likely cancerous. A biopsy later confirmed high-grade astrocytoma with piloid features, or HGAP, a rare and aggressive primary central nervous system tumor, per the same account. HGAP is not an old diagnosis so much as a newly sorted one. The tumor type was only formally added to the World Health Organization's Classification of Central Nervous System Tumors in 2021, when researchers began relying on DNA methylation profiling — a way of reading a tumor's molecular fingerprint rather than just its appearance under a microscope — to classify brain cancers, according to research published in A clinical study of 421 patients published in Neuro-Oncology this month reported a median overall survival of 88 months — about 7.3 years — among people with HGAP. Older age and alterations in the ATRX gene were identified as negative prognostic factors, according to . The study also found that HGAP predominantly affects adults, with a median diagnostic age of 46 years, making Rowan's diagnosis at 22 unusually young in comparison with the study population. The Central Brain Tumor Registry of the United States notes that primary brain and central nervous system tumors affect tens of thousands of Americans each year, per . In Utah, primary malignant central nervous system tumors are tracked through the Utah Cancer Registry. Before starting treatment, Rowan had her eggs retrieved and frozen, completing the IVF process through Huntsman, per KSL News. The Huntsman Cancer Institute's Adolescent and Young Adult Cancer Program coordinates oncofertility navigation and fertility preservation, including egg banking, for cancer patients ages 15 to 39, according to . Huntsman also offers cancer-related grant programs, the station's report notes. Rowan then began 6.5 weeks of radiation and 12 rounds of chemotherapy. HGAP-specific population rates are not provided by the broad cancer statistics available here. The Central Brain Tumor Registry of the United States reported an average annual rate of 26.05 new primary malignant and non-malignant brain and other central nervous system tumors per 100,000 people in the United States, based on 2018–2022 data. Separate mortality data for brain and other nervous system cancer are not represented by this incidence figure. Those figures include broader tumor categories and do not represent a rate specific to HGAP. Fertility can be a treatment-planning issue for young patients: the lists central nervous system tumors among cancers in young people that can be associated with fertility-related problems. Whether to exercise during and after cancer treatment, including marathon training, depends on individual medical circumstances. Running remained part of Rowan's routine during treatment. In September 2025, while receiving chemotherapy and radiation, she ran the Big Cottonwood Marathon, her first marathon. The REVEL Big Cottonwood Marathon course drops roughly 5,200 feet in elevation from Guardsman Pass through Big Cottonwood Canyon into Murray, making it one of the fastest downhill marathon courses in the state, according to the . Rowan has also run several half marathons and describes herself as a weight-lifter as well as a runner. articles.title: Stock market shrugs off geopolitical risk as UBS says drawdowns are short-lived: Chart of the Day
articles.desc: Geopolitics may have dominated headlines over the past year, but the stock market has remained resilient.
articles.content: Stock market shrugs off geopolitical risk as UBS says drawdowns are short-lived: Chart of the Day Stock market shrugs off geopolitical risk as UBS says drawdowns are short-lived: Chart of the Day For investors watching the markets over the past year, geopolitics have been In April 2025, President Trump announced a that set off a redefinition of global trade relations. In February 2026, the US and Israel launched , now in its sixth month. In Eastern Europe, the war in Ukraine rages into its fifth year, while Canada may move to become the European Union's first "associate member." But that apparent level of risk doesn't always portend ill for the stock market, UBS Wealth Management chief investment officer Mark Haefele argued in a note to clients on Friday. "The challenge for investors is that they must make two forecasts at once," Haefele said. "First, whether a geopolitical event will prove economically significant, and second, whether the consequences are already reflected in asset prices." "History suggests that both forecasts are harder to make than they might seem," Haefele wrote. The war in Iran, especially, has proven far more complicated and long-lasting than expected. Initially pitched by the White House as a two-week excursion, the conflict is now into its seventh month and has spent that time roiling the energy market. How to protect your money as Mideast turmoil fuels market volatility While oil prices have come slightly off their wartime highs set early in the conflict, benchmark Brent ( ) contracts have continued to hold at or above $100 as the Strait of Hormuz — the world's most critical chokepoint for global energy flows — remains unsafe for shipping. In recent days, Houthi activity along the Red Sea and attacks on critical Saudi infrastructure have opened up a new front in the war. The complexity of the conflict and the number of potential red lines for the White House that have been crossed — $100 oil, the 10-year Treasury yield above 5% — led strategists at they couldn't forecast a clear path forward. "For the first time since the start of the Iran conflict, we don't have a baseline view," commodities strategists at JPMorgan, led by Natasha Kaneva, wrote to clients on Thursday. "We simply don't know how to model the endgame." remains just slightly off all-time highs as equities have largely shrugged off the war, with far more focus on earnings growth and the AI boom. That resilience matches the historical record. When the market does experience a geopolitical drawdown, Haefele said, they tend to be short-lived, measuring at a median of only 16 days. Since the attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941 that marked the entrance of the US into World War II, Haefele noted, the S&P 500 has been higher 12 months after the start of a geopolitical crisis roughly three-quarters of the time. In about half of the crisis incidents, the market recovered within a month. "Investors should also remember that geopolitical situations can change quickly — as we have seen many times in 2026," Haefele said, citing ceasefire agreements, increased oil production, and other potential shifts for the market. "In our view, investors should therefore be cautious about assuming that current geopolitical fears will persist indefinitely." articles.title: Scientists Unleash Franken-Mice With Brains That Are Nearly Half Human
articles.desc: Scientists grew mice with part of their brain missing and filled the gap with human neurons, resulting in brains that were nearly half human.
articles.content: Scientists Unleash Franken-Mice With Brains That Are Nearly Half Human | United States Pick countries on the world map and get breaking news alerts in your browser — free, no app. Scientists grew mice with part of their brain missing and filled the gap with human neurons, resulting in brains that were nearly half human. Scientists have created mice with brains that have millions of functioning human neurons fused into them. This groundbreaking feat could provide a new avenue for understanding and treating neurocognitive disorders, though the Frankenstein-esque nature of the work will surely raise ethical questions. , the Stanford University scientists report how they used genetic engineering to deliberately create mice with parts of their brain missing — namely a key region called the cortex. By also stripping the mice of the ability to replenish these cortex neurons, this carved out a space that they could implant human brain cells. Not only did the implanted human neurons take hold, but they multiplied dramatically, blooming from just a few hundred neurons to several million, and successfully connecting with the mouse brain. The mice themselves, meanwhile, largely behaved as normal, despite nearly half their brains now being human by volume. “For the past two decades, there’s been a quest to try to build models of the human brain outside of the human body,” senior author Sergiu Pașca, a Stanford professor of psychiatry who worked on the mice,. “This is not going to replace all the models we had before, but it’s going to provide us access to other aspects of human brain function that would be very difficult to study otherwise. ”— small clusters of human brain tissue that’re grown in a lab. The researchers used human skin cells and reprogrammed them so they would form the neurons found in the cortex. The cortex is significant, as it’s the “part of the brain that results in our humanness,” John Evans, a bioethicist at the University of California, San Diego, who was not involved in the study,The implanted human neurons weren’t mature, however, resembling those found in a third trimester fetus. While the mice largely moved and behaved as normal, they showed key human-like differences. When the researchers deprived baby mice with human neurons of oxygen around birth, they found that the rodents exhibited signs of brain damage. This is striking, because normal mouse pups exposed to low oxygen rarely face brain damage, while human babies often do. They also found that the human parts of the mice brains contained a long, specialized type of brain cell called a, which is only found in highly social animals like humans, apes, whales, and elephants. Crucially, von Economo neurons are some of the first brain cells to die in patients with a frontotemporal dementia, and their presence in the mice could help explore their role in the rare form of the disease. The project raises sensitive ethical considerations, though. Nita Farahany, professor of law and philosophy at Duke Law, drew attention to how the researchers cut off the experiments right when the brain cells reached six months old, which is before they could form further connections to the mouse brains. “They’re trying to stop the study before the markers of consciousness, or the fact of consciousness, might emerge,” Farhany told“Do you stop a study before an animal develops consciousness, if it has the potential or is on its way to develop consciousness? ” she continued. “Does it have different interests or rights that we would assign to it? ” We have summarized this news so that you can read it quickly. articles.title: Back To The Future's McFly Family Tree Across All 4 Time Periods Explained
articles.desc: The Back to the Future trilogy spans four eras of McFly history, from 1885 to 2015, revealing how each generation shaped Marty's story and future.
articles.content: Back To The Future's McFly Family Tree Across All 4 Time Periods Explained Richard Craig is a Senior Author at Screen Rant covering film and TV. Richard has also written extensively about horror and film soundtracks, contributing a chapter to the first major academic collection on the folk horror genre, . Richard is also a performing musician and holds an MA in Music and Sound Art. 's four major time periods is surprisingly extensive. Across (1990), Marty McFly's adventures take him to 1885, 1955, 1985, and 2015. While the trilogy is primarily remembered for its time-travel mechanics, the movies also spend a remarkable amount of time exploring Marty's family history. to show how personality traits, family relationships, and even recurring conflicts can echo across generations. One of the trilogy's running jokes is that seems to contain both a McFly and a Tannen. Whether it's George being bullied by Biff in 1955, Marty dealing with Biff's descendants in the future, or Seamus McFly crossing paths with Buford "Mad Dog" Tannen in the Old West, the families remain connected throughout history. The films also use casting to reinforce these connections. of the McFly family, while Lea Thompson portrays both Lorraine Baines McFly and Marty's great-great-grandmother. The result is a family tree that stretches from nineteenth-century Irish immigrants to Marty's own children living in the futuristic version of 2015 seen in Although several generations exist between the characters, every member helps explain how Marty became the person audiences follow throughout the trilogy. Some additional family members have since been added in games and the animated series, but these are not official canon and therefore have not been included here. as Marty's paternal great-great-grandfather. Living in Hill Valley in 1885, Seamus is among the earliest members of the family shown on screen and is portrayed by Michael J. Fox. He is married to Maggie McFly and is the father of William McFly. Seamus's name would be given to Marty as a middle name, presumably by George. Unlike later McFlys, Seamus refuses to be intimidated by Buford Tannen. His calm approach to conflict contrasts with the tendency of future generations to react when challenged. In many ways, he represents the version that Marty eventually learns to become by the end of Maggie McFly is Marty's paternal great-great-grandmother and is played by Lea Thompson. She is the wife of Seamus McFly and mother of William McFly. Her most notable feature is her resemblance to Lorraine Baines McFly, who is also played by Thompson. While Maggie is not biologically related to Lorraine, franchise co-creator Bob Gale jokingly explained that McFly men appear genetically predisposed to be attracted to women who resemble Maggie. Her presence also helps create a visual link between the 1885 and 1985 storylines. Seeing Thompson in both roles reinforces the cyclical nature of the McFly family's history. Although Martin McFly never physically appears in the trilogy, he remains an important figure in the family's history. He is Seamus McFly's brother and therefore Marty's great-great-great-uncle. According to Seamus, Martin was stabbed to death during a confrontation before the events of Martin was killed because he refused to back down from a confrontation in case anybody thought he was a coward. This is introduced as a major plot for Marty McFly in . Learning of Martin’s death gave Marty the drive to finally buck this trend and improve his future in William "Willie" McFly is the son of Seamus and Maggie and the great-grandfather of Marty McFly (and therefore the grandfather of George McFly). In , William appears only as an infant living on the McFly farm in 1885, and as an adult in a photograph. As an adult, he is likewise played by Michael J. Fox, with Marty commenting on his good looks. Despite his limited screen time, William occupies an important position within the family tree. He serves as the bridge between t

articles.title: Strange Seeds Appear to Be Growing Into Massive Black Holes
articles.desc: Could this explain the "little red dots" mystery? The post Strange Seeds Appear to Be Growing Into Massive Black Holes appeared first on Futurism .
articles.content: Strange Seeds Appear to Be Growing Into Massive Black Holes puzzled by the existence of “little red dots ” first showing up in observations by NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope. These objects appeared in a region they believe dates to just hundreds of millions of years after the Big Bang, one of the oldest known neighborhoods of the universe. Several possible explanations have since emerged, with some arguing they could be emerging galaxies. Others suggested that the red dots could be the earliest stages of supermassive black holes, which are enormous cosmic objects that have gravitationally collapsed and are often lurking at the center of galaxies. this week, Max Planck Institute astrophysicist Sunmyon Chon and his colleagues delve into this possibility by simulating the earliest stages of the universe. They found that the rapidly-forming black holes could be emitting light while accreting material, appearing as the mysterious red dots, or “seeds,” picked up by the James Webb. Despite lurking pretty much everywhere we look in our known universe, the nature of black holes remains mysterious. Scientists are still actively exploring new types of them, leaving the possibility that the red dots could be a kind we have yet to characterize. Chon and his colleagues propose that the newly-formed “overmassive” black holes “rapidly develop dense, optically thick disks whose strong electron scattering produces broad [hydrogen-alpha] emission comparable to that seen in little red dots.” Hydrogen-alpha is a specific visible spectral line in astronomical observations that focuses on a specific deep-red part of the spectrum. Chon’s team suggests that these black holes evolve into “overmassive” quasars — extremely bright celestial objects that are powered by gas being absorbed by a supermassive black hole — that were detected by the James Webb. The scientists posit they could be the “progenitors of today’s supermassive black holes,” in an evolutionary process they suggest could take less than a billion years. “At 500,000 years, it looks like a little red dot, but after maybe one million years or so, the surrounding gas is mostly accreted into the black hole,” Chon While the broader scientific community has yet to come to a consensus, some aren’t convinced. For instance, University of Cambridge astrophysicist Roberto Maiolino told the that he prefers a more familiar explanation. He suggests the red dots are simply part of the evolution of a regular black holes. And Chon remains very open-minded about the viability of his theory. “We don’t want to claim that all the little red dots come from what we’ve modeled,” he told the newspaper. “So many new kinds of findings are coming out and it’s good news for new simulations.” Astronomers Discover an Entirely New Type of Object: a “Black Hole Star”

articles.content: MINNEAPOLIS--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Apogee Enterprises, Inc. (Nasdaq: APOG), a leading provider of architectural building products and services, as well as high-performance coated materials used in a variety of applications, today announced the completion of its previously announced acquisition of SIA “GroGlass” ("Groglass").
